title: Knowledge Graph Node
description: A single teachable concept in the Maths knowledge graph. IDs come from kg/spine.json and are immutable.

description.description: 2-4 sentences: what the concept is and why it matters, student-readable.

oneOf.description: Legacy bare id (treated as strength: hard).

strength.description: hard = gates unlocking (mastery required first); soft = strongly recommended, helps but does not block.

reason.description: One plain-language line a student can read: WHY this comes first, e.g. 'You can't compare decimals until place value is solid.'

prerequisites.description: Node IDs from kg/spine.json that should be mastered first. Only true conceptual prerequisites. Typed form preferred: hard edges gate, soft edges recommend, and every edge carries a student-readable reason.

parent_check.description: One question/activity a parent (no maths background) can run at home in 2 minutes to sense whether the child owns this concept. Written to the parent, warm, concrete. Feeds /digest.

ncert.description: Mapping to the NCERT textbook chapter(s) covering this node.

ccss.description: Common Core State Standards codes this node aligns with, e.g. 6.RP.A.1, HSA-REI.B.4. Empty array if no clean alignment.

learning_outcomes.description: Observable 'can-do' statements used as the mastery checklist.

id.description: Unique within the node; referenced by question distractors.

description.description: The faulty mental model, e.g. 'multiplication always makes numbers bigger'.

signal.description: What a student who holds this misconception typically does or says.

remedy.description: The teaching move that best repairs this specific misconception.

est_minutes.description: Typical minutes to first mastery for an on-grade student.

modalities.description: Modalities that work especially well for THIS concept, best-first.

thinking_routines.description: Routine IDs from harness/rules/20-thinking-routines.md that fit this concept, e.g. 'see-think-wonder', 'claim-support-question'.

real_world_hooks.description: Concrete contexts that make this concept feel real (cricket scores, cooking, money, games...).

video_search.description: A good YouTube search query for this concept (do not hardcode URLs; they rot).

misconception.description: The misconception id (m1...) in this node that choosing this distractor reveals. REQUIRED on every incorrect option unless diagnosis explains a slip instead.

diagnosis.description: What choosing this option tells us about the student's thinking (e.g. 'careless sign slip, concept likely intact').

options.description: Exactly 4 options, exactly 1 correct. Every wrong option MUST be engineered to catch a specific error - never random fillers.

explanation.description: Full worked solution shown after answering.
